outcome.answer: For chatbots handling conversational noise, attention pooling improved intent-classification F1 over alternative pooling strategies in experiments on BANKING77 and CLINC150; mean pooling degraded performance, while last-token pooling was recommended for clean queries [2]. For robustness to mixed-intent and adversarial prompts, training-free methods were generally more robust than training-based classifiers, though training-based methods had an advantage on harder distinctions such as Java versus Python [3]. For systems that must detect unfamiliar intents, EliDecide uses flexible ellipsoid boundaries and reports strong open-intent detection results [4].
